meta.one_line: Editorial structure for 'A duel became a crowd': the US/USSR launch duopoly (99% -> 54.5% share) pluralized into a crowd led by China and a new commercial sector, even as the all-time ledger stays 85.5% old-world. Change is in WHO launches, not how much.

core_claim: Spaceflight stopped being a two-country contest: the US/USSR duopoly that launched ~99% of everything thinned to 54.5% as China (riding one rocket family) and a new commercial/startup sector crowded in -- yet the cumulative ledger is still 85.5% old-world. The change is in WHO launches, not how much.

edt_01.label: The year the table flipped
edt_01.title: The year the table flipped
edt_01.editorial_notes: Lead with the 2018 China crossover as the premise (the Economist headline), then prime the hero in edt_03 WITHOUT giving its number. State the 1960s ~99% as the SETUP, not 54.5%. Census-authority line builds trust (5,726 attempts, 94.0% success, Sputnik 1957). [MEDIA: audio] = the mandatory top-of-article BGM now-playing card; an opening Long March image also belongs here. Do not state the partial-2018 raw 28-27 here (save for edt_04/05, where it is marked partial).

edt_02.label: Two superpowers and a workhorse
edt_02.title: Two superpowers and a workhorse
edt_02.editorial_notes: Establish the duel and Soviet dominance. Exact: Soviet 1982 peak = 108 of 129; Soyuz-U 632 (most-flown single vehicle); decade volume peak 1970s 1,226 then 1980s 1,191 -> 1990s 889 -> 2000s 650 trough. SU code vanishes after 1991. [CHART: ana_03] is the master per-country-year spine the whole piece references. Merge SU+RU into one 'USSR/Russia' series.

edt_03.label: It's who, not how much
edt_03.title: It's who, not how much
edt_03.editorial_notes: THE THESIS TURN and the HERO's home. ana_02 sets up 'volume is flat' (peak year 1967=139; 2018=80 PARTIAL vs 114 full-year). The hero year-scrubber sits ABOVE the reveal paragraph: the reader produces the duopoly share falling ~99% -> 54.5% (HHI ~6,600 -> ~2,200; 2 -> 7 countries) before the prose states it. The US 'never collapsed' framing must survive. ana_06 supplies the 'no bloc holds a majority in the 2010s, first time since the 1950s' line.

edt_04.label: The new contender, part one - a nation
edt_04.title: The new contender, part one - a nation
edt_04.editorial_notes: China's decade ramp 13/15/39/64/171. CROSSOVER MUST BE PARTIAL-MARKED: dataset partial (Jan-Oct) China 28 > USA 27 > Russia 10; full-year external 39/34/20. Never present 28-27 as a final tally. China = 287 of 302 (95.0%) Long March (the guess_then_reveal interactive). Detective scout_brief: Long March launch photo/clip belongs here.

edt_05.label: Does the crossover survive the caveat?
edt_05.title: Does the crossover survive the caveat?
edt_05.editorial_notes: LOAD-BEARING credibility beat ('earn the trust') AND the visible-prose home of the lead's material limitation (partial 2018). Keep det_11 + the partial caveat in the prose. The crossover holds at partial (28-27), naive annualize (~33.6 vs 32.4) and external full-year (39-34); China is #1 in exactly one of 62 years. State honestly what it does NOT prove (a per-year count, not ownership of space). The annualize interactive lets the reader move months-elapsed against the real 39. Do not cut this section.

edt_06.label: But the old world still owns the ledger
edt_06.title: But the old world still owns the ledger
edt_06.editorial_notes: The COUNTER-TENSION (the honest twist that balances the hero). Cumulative: USSR/Russia 3,178 (55.5%) + USA 1,716 (30.0%) = 85.5%; Europe 307 edges China 302 all-time. Family scale gap: Soviet/Russian fleet >3,200 (R-7/Soyuz 1,832, Kosmos 621, Proton 411) vs Long March 287, Falcon 68. Hosts TWO distinct interactives (cumulative bar race ana_04 + vehicle-family treemap ana_13). [MEDIA: map] = static all-time country choropleth ONLY; NO point map (lat/long all blank) -- state this in prose.

edt_07.label: They are not cutting corners
edt_07.title: They are not cutting corners
edt_07.editorial_notes: Honest twist #2: newcomers are not trading reliability for entry. Country band: Europe 95.8 / China 95.7 / USSR-Russia 95.2 / USA 92.4 / Japan 92.2 / India 89.2; overall 94.0%. By type the surprise: private 97.4 > state 93.4 > startup 92.9 (startup on a thin 70-launch base -- note it). Maturation 46% (1950s) -> 97.1% peak (1980s) -> ~96%. The success-rate calculator (ana_10) is the interactive; ana_11/ana_09 are static callouts.

edt_08.label: The new contender, part two - a new kind of company
edt_08.title: The new contender, part two - a new kind of company
edt_08.editorial_notes: The second axis of 'new contenders' (a KIND, not a nation). Two waves: 'private' commercial from 1984 (Arianespace, peak 46.9% in 2000s) vs 'startup' appearing only 2006 (8.8% of 2010s). Startup class = SpaceX 68 (Falcon 9 62, Falcon 1 5, Falcon Heavy 1) + Rocket Lab 2; ramp 1 (2006) -> 19 (2017) -> 18 (partial 2018). Arianespace 260 (1984-2018). The guess_then_reveal startup-ramp is the interactive (ana_15). [MEDIA: video] = Falcon Heavy Feb-6-2018 embeddable instance per scout_brief. [CHART: ana_08] = agency-type stacked area.

edt_09.label: Two pictures of the same sky
edt_09.title: Two pictures of the same sky
edt_09.editorial_notes: Close on TENSION, not summary. Stakes: launch access = national power + a space economy ~$350bn (2016) -> $1tn+ (2040). End on the unresolved question: the per-year field is a crowd (54.5%, no majority), the all-time ledger is still a duel won long ago (85.5% old-world) -- which is the future? Do not resolve it.

hero.why_hero: The single contestable headline the reader must produce: drag a year 1957->2018 and the two-superpower combined share falls under your hand from ~99% to 54.5% while the per-country bars re-rank beneath it (merges img_01's share-collapse with img_02's launch-race over one launchSnapshot model). It is the thesis ('a duel became a crowd') made hands-on, and it surfaces the exact per-year duopoly share so the standfirst can prime the question without spoiling the number.

supporting.earns_place: Distinct finding = the all-time cumulative ledger (advance the year and produce the ranking ending USSR/Russia 3,178 > USA 1,716 > Europe 307 > China 302 = 85.5% old-world). It is the COUNTER-TENSION to the hero's per-year crowd, not a duplicate: the hero shows the field pluralizing per year, this shows history unrewritten.

Distinct finding = the partial-2018 validation. The reader sets months-elapsed and produces China's naive full-year pro-rate (28 -> ~33.6) against the external actual 39, verifying the crossover survives truncation. It is the credibility keystone for the lead and teaches a number no other widget does.

Distinct finding = success rate by country (pick a country, produce its rate; China 95.7% ties the incumbents). Rebuts the 'cheap volume / cutting corners' read -- a reliability finding distinct from every count/share widget.

Distinct finding = China's single-family concentration (guess the share, then meet 287 of 302 = 95% Long March). Distinct from the country-count story: it shows China's rise IS one sovereign rocket family, vs the diversified US fleet.

Distinct finding = the startup ramp (guess the year a 'startup' first reached orbit, then watch SpaceX/Rocket Lab climb 1 (2006) -> 19 (2017) -> 18 (partial 2018)). Opens the SECOND axis of 'new contenders' -- a new KIND of actor, not a new nation -- which no country-based widget covers.

Distinct finding = the vehicle-FAMILY scale gap (explore a treemap and produce R-7/Soyuz 1,832 and a >3,200 Soviet fleet vs Long March 287, Falcon 68). Hardware mass, distinct from ana_04's launch-count ledger and ana_14's China-internal share; cut first if scope must trim.
